chunks: “Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, spread the earth from beneath the Kaaba to Mina, then spread it from Mina to Arafat, then spread it from Arafat to Mina. So the earth is from Arafat, and Arafat is from Mina, and Mina is from the Kaaba. Likewise, our knowledge is part of itself from part.”

key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: the Kaaba, the sacred center in Mecca
key_terms.بَعْضُهُ مِنْ بَعْضٍ: part of it derives from part, indicating connected transmission
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the well-known plain of hajj
key_terms.عِلْمُنَا: our knowledge, referring to the knowledge of the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, one of the sacred sites of hajj

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام relate the sacred geography of the Kaaba, Mina, and Arafat to the knowledge of the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام describes the spreading of the earth in relation to the sacred sites of the hajj, beginning from beneath the Kaaba and extending through Mina and Arafat. He then draws a parallel between this sacred ordering and the transmission of the knowledge of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, each part deriving from the other.
